title: Sector traffic and dependent addresses
question: Why can equal useful payload require different sector traffic?
scope: Illustrative 4-byte words and aligned 16-byte sectors; cold cache, merged requests, no reuse. Separate pointer example excludes its traffic from request-set metrics.

objects.label: Address space: one row per aligned sector
Fetched sectors for the four requests

steps.title: Establish the cold request set
steps.explanation: Each request reads one four-byte word. No reuse or prefetch is modeled.

snapshot.result: Adjacent words can share a sector; separated words may require distinct sectors.

steps.title: Fetch one aligned sector
steps.explanation: The interface fetches the entire sector and merges requests inside it.

snapshot.result: Fetched sectors retain source words; unused bytes still count as traffic.

transition.meaning: The interface fetches the entire sector and merges requests inside it.

steps.title: Resolve the separate payload address
steps.explanation: An index read returns byte address 48. The payload read could not issue earlier.

snapshot.result: Address 48 is now available; the dependent read may issue next.

transition.meaning: An index read returns byte address 48. The payload read could not issue earlier.

steps.title: Read the dependent payload
steps.explanation: The resolved address now permits the payload request, regardless of unused bandwidth.

snapshot.result: The payload becomes readable only after its address is known.

transition.meaning: The resolved address now permits the payload request, regardless of unused bandwidth.

invariants: Sector fetches do not consume or alter source words.
Pointer resolution must precede the dependent payload request.

title: Retain C across reduction tiles
question: What must remain resident when operand tiles are replaced?
scope: Declared 2×2 integer GEMM with 2×1 A and 1×2 B slices; local capacity holds both operands and four C accumulators. Counts are elements, not a runtime prediction.

steps.title: Establish a local C tile
steps.explanation: Two operand elements from each matrix fit beside the retained four-element C tile.

snapshot.result: Resident operand slices can be reused across all four output accumulators.

steps.title: Load reduction slice k=0
steps.explanation: Two operand elements from each matrix fit beside the retained four-element C tile.

snapshot.result: Resident operand slices can be reused across all four output accumulators.

transition.meaning: Two operand elements from each matrix fit beside the retained four-element C tile.

steps.title: Accumulate slice k=0
steps.explanation: One local outer product updates all four C accumulators.

snapshot.result: The first products remain local so the next slice can add to them.

transition.meaning: One local outer product updates all four C accumulators.

steps.title: Replace operands with slice k=1
steps.explanation: Only operand slices are replaced; the local C tile retains every earlier contribution.

snapshot.result: Replacing operands preserves every contribution already accumulated in C.

transition.meaning: Only operand slices are replaced; the local C tile retains every earlier contribution.

steps.title: Accumulate slice k=1 into retained C
steps.explanation: One local outer product updates all four C accumulators.

snapshot.result: Both reduction slices have contributed; the complete C tile can now be written.

transition.meaning: One local outer product updates all four C accumulators.

steps.title: Write the completed C tile
steps.explanation: The full reduction must finish before the C tile is written.

snapshot.result: Backing memory now receives the complete C tile; earlier partial sums were never written out.

transition.meaning: The full reduction must finish before the C tile is written.

invariants: Replacing A/B slices preserves the accumulated C tile.
Backing memory receives C only after the complete reduction.

title: Logical order survives scattered placement
question: How does an ordered sequence use noncontiguous blocks safely?
scope: Source eight-block pool, equal block sizes, requests C/D/E, no prefix sharing. E has four pages and a partially filled final block; paging does not change KV bytes per token.

objects.label: Request E: logical pages in token order
E block table: logical index → physical block
Query, resolved block, and KV read

steps.title: Inspect the fragmented free pool
steps.explanation: C and D leave free blocks in two separated runs. E needs four equal-size blocks.

snapshot.result: Four free blocks exist, but they do not form one contiguous run.

steps.title: Allocate E’s four page mappings
steps.explanation: Assign E logical pages to physical blocks 0, 1, 4, and 5. The partially filled last block remains allocated.

snapshot.result: E’s logical order is preserved even though its physical blocks are separated.

transition.meaning: Assign E logical pages to physical blocks 0, 1, 4, and 5. The partially filled last block remains allocated.

steps.title: Resolve E logical page 2 to block 4
steps.explanation: Resolve logical page 2 through E’s table entry 2; it names physical block 4.

snapshot.result: Logical page 2 skips C’s blocks because E’s table names block 4.

transition.meaning: Resolve logical page 2 through E’s table entry 2; it names physical block 4.

steps.title: Read E logical page 2
steps.explanation: Read physical block 4 using the resolved table value. The source block remains resident.

snapshot.result: The query receives a copy; E’s original block remains allocated.

transition.meaning: Read physical block 4 using the resolved table value. The source block remains resident.

steps.title: Finish E’s pending access
steps.explanation: The final E access finishes. No in-flight E reader remains, but E still owns its blocks.

snapshot.result: E can now release its blocks because its pending access has finished.

transition.meaning: The final E access finishes. No in-flight E reader remains, but E still owns its blocks.

steps.title: Release E’s blocks and mappings
steps.explanation: Return only E’s unshared blocks to the free pool and invalidate E’s mappings.

snapshot.result: C and D retain their original blocks; E’s former blocks can serve another request.

transition.meaning: Return only E’s unshared blocks to the free pool and invalidate E’s mappings.

invariants: The E table maps logical page 2 to physical block 4.
A read preserves the block and its ownership.
E blocks become free only after its last access; C and D never move.

title: Rollback consumes resident capacity
question: Why can retraining block an additional loaded model copy?
scope: Source node has eight accelerator slots: serving and immediate rollback use two each; retraining uses four, then a canary uses two. The chapter’s six-hour run duration is outside this capacity-only lifecycle view.

objects.label: Eight accelerator slots on one node
Persistent candidate artifact outside accelerator slots

steps.title: Keep serving and rollback resident
steps.explanation: Serving and the immediate-rollback copy are already resident.

snapshot.result: Immediate rollback reserves resident capacity before retraining begins.

steps.title: Allocate the retraining job
steps.explanation: The retraining run occupies the remaining four slots and leaves no room for another loaded copy.

snapshot.result: The node is full; another loaded copy cannot fit while retraining runs.

transition.meaning: The retraining run occupies the remaining four slots and leaves no room for another loaded copy.

steps.title: Persist the completed candidate
steps.explanation: Retraining persists its candidate outside accelerator residency. Its device allocations still require release.

snapshot.result: The candidate exists persistently, but training still occupies its device slots.

transition.meaning: Retraining persists its candidate outside accelerator residency. Its device allocations still require release.

steps.title: Release completed training allocations
steps.explanation: The completed retraining job releases its four slots after its last device access.

snapshot.result: Freed training slots can now hold a candidate without evicting the hot standby.

transition.meaning: The completed retraining job releases its four slots after its last device access.

steps.title: Load the candidate canary
steps.explanation: Load the candidate canary into two freed slots; the existing hot standby remains available.

snapshot.result: Canary and hot standby coexist; two slots remain free under this schedule.

transition.meaning: Load the candidate canary into two freed slots; the existing hot standby remains available.

invariants: Serving and hot standby remain resident through the whole schedule.
